# Social cards — provenance

Three rasters ship from this directory and are referenced as `og:image`:

| file | used by |
| --- | --- |
| `default.png` | every page without a card of its own |
| `remote-mcp-fastmcp.png` | `/posts/remote-mcp-fastmcp/` |
| `vibe-coding.png` | `/posts/vibe-coding/` |

**These are produced, not generated by an image model.** `tools/og-card.mjs`
builds each card as HTML in the site's own design system and renders it with
Chrome; the PNG is the browser's render of that markup. `npm run og`
regenerates all three.

They are named by **URL slug**, so a page finds its own card through
`page.fileSlug` via the `ogCard` filter in `eleventy.config.js`. A page with no
card of its own falls back to `default.png`. Adding a card for a new post means
adding one entry to `CARDS` in the tool and re-running it.

og:image must be a raster — no social platform renders SVG — which is why this
is rendered output rather than an SVG with the rest of the site's assets.

## Regenerating

```bash
npm run og     # rewrites all three PNGs
```

Chrome is needed only to render. The cards are committed, so a deploy never
depends on the renderer being present.

## Provenance

The generation record for each raster is embedded in the PNG itself, and its
text lives at `tools/og-card.prompt.txt`. After re-rendering a card, re-embed
it so the raster is not orphaned:

```bash
impeccable embed-prompt assets/og/<card>.png --prompt-file tools/og-card.prompt.txt
impeccable embed-prompt --scan assets/og     # should report 0 missing
```
